institutionName: Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Brazil because I had visited before and loved it there. What made the experience even more appealing was the opportunity to learn a new language alongside my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: PUC provided clear and helpful information upon arrival, and their guidance was generally very good. However, some parts of the process took place quite late, which caused a certain level of stress, although everything ultimately worked out. On the other hand, the information from KU was less clear, and the partnership agreement was finalized just before the application deadline. As a result, I had to pay a higher tuition fee.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, a bus picked me up at the airport, and the following day there was an introduction session at PUC. Overall, the assistance provided was very good and made the transition smooth.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find off-campus housing. I initially stayed in an Airbnb, which gave me time to look for something more permanent. Afterward, I moved in with two other PUC students. I would recommend starting with short-term accommodation and then searching locally once you arrive. I would also not recommend Uliving, as friends of mine stayed there and found it expensive, with a mandatory five-month lease that limited flexibility.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no on-campus housing available, so all students live off campus. Homestays had mixed reviews, some students had positive experiences, but most of the people I know eventually chose to move out and find other accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process took place relatively late and you have to be fast to get the subjects that you want. I would strongly recommend being quick during registration and deciding on alternative subjects in advance in case your first choices are unavailable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: PUC was very helpful and provided support when needed, including assisting students with enrollment in classes when necessary.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted but had more classes than recommended since my mandatory Portuguese lessons where not part of ECTS in Denmark.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise future exchange students to be prepared for a late registration process and to act quickly once registration opens. It is important to have alternative courses in mind in case your preferred subjects are full, and to stay in contact with the host institution, as they are generally helpful with enrollment issues.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: PUC does not offer many master’s-level courses, as the bachelor’s programs are significantly longer than in Denmark. However, this worked out well, and I was able to take several interesting bachelor-level courses, all of which were approved by my home institution.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to UCPH, the teaching style involved more sitting and listening, with less student engagement during classes. However, several courses included field tours, which added a practical dimension to the learning experience. The academic level was generally good, and some exams were handwritten and conducted in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Brazilian Foreign Policy I, as it provides valuable insight into Brazil’s role in international realtions and their shifting policies. I would also highly recommend INT Area Studies III - Art & Resistance in Latin America, which offers a unique interdisciplinary perspective on Latin American history, culture, and political resistance through art

questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Way more expensive than expected. Luckily I received a lot of scholarships.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities were available, including different sports and many social events for students. However, I did not participate extensively, so my knowledge of the specific activities offered is somewhat limited.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking part in social events and activities organized for exchange students, as they are a great way to meet people and become part of the student community. I would also encourage students to explore the city and Brazilian culture outside of campus, as this is a big part of the exchange experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I’d recommend visiting São Paulo and Ilha Grande, but honestly there’s already so much to see and do in Rio de Janeiro that you can easily spend most weekends just exploring the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to adjust to the local culture. People were very welcoming, and spending time in the city helped me feel comfortable quickly, even though some cultural differences took a bit of time to get used to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend being open and proactive, as local students are generally very welcoming. Joining group activities, talking to people in class, and making an effort to learn and use Portuguese all helped a lot.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Safety was the most challenging cultural difference for me, particularly the need to be more cautious and avoid walking alone at night.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really loved the culture. The samba, the overall vibe, and the energy of the city made living there an amazing experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First, don’t be too scared, it is just a big city. Second, be flexible and open-minded, especially with courses and housing. Third, take advantage of the experience outside of academics by exploring the city and engaging with the local culture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Things may feel a bit unstructured at times, especially in the beginning, but it usually works out. Patience and flexibility are important. Learning some basic Portuguese before arriving is very helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the friendships I made, the experiences I had, gaining a deeper understanding of South America, and learning a new language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was the process of starting over in a new place, which could be both mentally and emotionally draining at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
